transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I’m here because lately whenever I have to get near a scaffold, a roof edge, or any kind of upper platform, I get this feeling like I’m about to go over. Even when I can see the rails are there and I know it’s supposed to be safe, my head just keeps telling me I’m going to fall.
Is this fear limited to heights, or do you experience similar feelings in other situations as well?

It’s really just with heights, as far as I can tell. Like scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms—that’s when it hits me. Even if the rails are there and I know it should be safe, my mind keeps saying I’m about to fall.
When you feel this way around heights, do you find yourself avoiding those situations altogether or going through them with a lot of distress?

Yeah, I avoid it a lot now. I’ve been handing off the height inspections to my foremen when I can, and I’ll move meetings down to ground level instead of going up. If I absolutely have to go up, I make sure someone stays right beside me, and I just rush through it scared the whole time.
Do you feel that your fear of being near heights is excessive or unreasonable, or does it feel like a natural reaction to a dangerous situation?

It feels excessive, yeah. I mean, I know the rails are there and the setup is supposed to be safe, but as soon as I’m near a scaffold or a roof edge, my head just tells me I’m about to go over. It doesn’t feel like a normal caution thing anymore.
When you’re near heights or thinking about being near heights, do you ever experience sudden episodes of intense fear or panic, like your heart racing, sweating, or feeling like you can’t breathe?

Yeah. It comes on pretty fast. The second I step onto temporary stairs, or even just start walking toward an open upper floor, my chest tightens up and my hands get wet. Sometimes my legs feel like they’re going to lock up before I can even make myself take another step.
When you're near heights and feeling afraid, is your main worry that you might actually fall, or is it more of a general sense of danger or panic without a clear focus?

It’s mostly that I’m going to fall. Like, even if I can see the rails are there and I know it’s supposed to be safe, once I’m near a scaffold or a roof edge or an upper platform, my head just goes straight to, “I’m about to go over.” It’s not just vague panic — it’s really focused on falling.
